BSI C5 Criterion: OIS-01 Information Security Management System (ISMS)
rationale: OIS-01 requires top management to operate, resource and continually improve an ISMS covering the cloud service. Top Management Commitment provides the visible leadership, resourcing and direction that keep the ISMS running.

BSI C5 Criterion: OIS-01 Information Security Management System (ISMS)
rationale: OIS-01 requires defined responsibilities and governance bodies within the ISMS. Charters & Committees establishes the chartered oversight bodies that carry out that governance.

BSI C5 Criterion: OIS-01 Information Security Management System (ISMS)
rationale: OIS-01 requires structured management of information security objectives and risks. The Security Oversight Committee provides the governance body that prioritises and reviews the security programme.

BSI C5 Criterion: OIS-04 Segregation of Duties
rationale: OIS-04 requires conflicting duties and areas of responsibility to be separated. Identity Management enforces least privilege and separation of duties in role design and access assignment.

BSI C5 Criterion: OIS-05 Contact with Relevant Government Agencies and Interest Groups
rationale: OIS-05 requires maintained contacts with authorities and special-interest groups to stay informed about threats and obligations. Information-Sharing Communities maintains those peer and ISAC relationships and exchanges sanitised threat intelligence.

BSI C5 Criterion: OIS-05 Contact with Relevant Government Agencies and Interest Groups
rationale: OIS-05 requires established contacts with relevant government agencies. Law Enforcement Partners maintains the procedures and relationships for engaging authorities when criminal activity is suspected.

BSI C5 Criterion: OPS-23 Managing Vulnerabilities, Malfunctions and Errors - System Hardening
rationale: OPS-23 requires systems to be hardened against known attack vectors using documented, approved configuration baselines. Security Standards defines those enforceable hardening baselines, which P.PS then applies to the platform.

BSI C5 Criterion: OIS-06 Risk Management Policy
rationale: OIS-06 requires a documented risk management policy that defines how risks are identified, assessed and treated. The Risk Management Framework establishes that unified enterprise risk method.

BSI C5 Criterion: OIS-07 Application of the Risk Management Policy
rationale: OIS-07 requires the risk management policy to be applied to the cloud service, with risks assessed and treated at defined intervals. The Cybersecurity Risk-Management Program continuously identifies, analyses and treats cyber risk under that policy.

BSI C5 Criterion: OIS-07 Application of the Risk Management Policy
rationale: OIS-07 requires regular risk assessments and risk treatment plans with owners and deadlines. Cybersecurity Risk Management runs the ongoing evaluation of threats, vulnerabilities and exposure that produces those assessments.

BSI C5 Criterion: OIS-07 Application of the Risk Management Policy
rationale: OIS-07 includes risks arising from subservice organisations and suppliers in the risk assessment. The Third-Party Risk-Management Program identifies and manages the risk that vendors pose to data and systems.

BSI C5 Criterion: SP-01 Documentation, Communication and Provision of Policies and Instructions
rationale: SP-01 requires policies and instructions to be documented, communicated and made available to those who must apply them. Core Policies establishes and governs the policy suite and its communication.

BSI C5 Criterion: SP-02 Review and Approval of Policies and Instructions
rationale: SP-02 requires policies to be reviewed and approved by authorised bodies at least annually and when changes occur. Security Policies defines the enforceable information security expectations and their review cycle.

BSI C5 Criterion: SP-03 Exceptions from Existing Policies and Instructions
rationale: SP-03 requires exceptions to policies to be documented, approved and reviewed. Core Standards turns policy into auditable requirements and governs documented, time-limited exceptions.

BSI C5 Criterion: HR-01 Verification of Qualification and Trustworthiness
rationale: HR-01 requires background and qualification checks on internal and external employees before access is granted. Human Resources runs the screening practices that uphold confidentiality and integrity.

BSI C5 Criterion: HR-02 Employment Terms and Conditions
rationale: HR-02 requires employment contracts to set out information security responsibilities. HR Policies defines the personnel rules that support secure and responsible conduct through the employment lifecycle.

BSI C5 Criterion: HR-03 Security Training and Awareness Programme
rationale: HR-03 requires a security awareness and training programme for all personnel, repeated regularly. Cybersecurity Training delivers foundational and role-based security awareness to counter phishing, social engineering and insider threats.

BSI C5 Criterion: HR-04 Disciplinary Measures
rationale: HR-04 requires a disciplinary process for violations of security policies. HR Policies sets the consequences for non-compliance within the employee lifecycle.

BSI C5 Criterion: HR-05 Responsibilities in the Event of Termination or Change of Employment
rationale: HR-05 requires defined responsibilities for termination and role changes, including return of assets and withdrawal of access. Human Resources manages departures and role changes so that those steps are completed.

BSI C5 Criterion: HR-06 Confidentiality Agreements
rationale: HR-06 requires confidentiality or non-disclosure agreements with internal and external employees. Human Resources maintains those agreements as part of onboarding and contract management.

BSI C5 Criterion: AM-01 Asset Inventory
rationale: AM-01 requires an inventory of all assets used to provide the cloud service, with owners and attributes. System Asset Management maintains the authoritative, classified and owned asset inventory.

BSI C5 Criterion: AM-02 Acceptable Use and Safe Handling of Assets Policy
rationale: AM-02 requires a policy for the acceptable use and safe handling of assets. COC: Acceptable Use sets the rules personnel must follow for appropriate use of systems and data.

BSI C5 Criterion: AM-03 Commissioning of Hardware
rationale: AM-03 requires hardware to be approved and recorded before commissioning. System Asset Management records commissioned hardware in the inventory with ownership and classification.

BSI C5 Criterion: AM-04 Decommissioning of Hardware
rationale: AM-04 requires data on hardware to be securely erased or the media destroyed before decommissioning. Classification & Handling defines the handling and sanitisation protocols for media based on data sensitivity.

BSI C5 Criterion: AM-05 Commitment to Permissible Use, Safe Handling and Return of Assets
rationale: AM-05 requires personnel to commit to permissible use and return of assets. COC: Acceptable Use obtains personnel acknowledgement of the rules for use and return of organisational assets.

BSI C5 Criterion: AM-06 Asset Classification and Labelling
rationale: AM-06 requires assets to be classified and labelled according to a classification scheme. Classification & Handling applies the classification labels and matching handling rules.

BSI C5 Criterion: PS-01 Physical Security and Environmental Control Requirements
rationale: PS-01 requires documented requirements for physical security and environmental controls at data centre locations. Environment Controls protects assets against environmental hazards and facility failures.

BSI C5 Criterion: PS-02 Redundancy Model
rationale: PS-02 requires a redundancy model so that failures of individual components do not interrupt the service. Resilience Controls engineers systems to absorb and recover from disruptive events.

BSI C5 Criterion: PS-03 Perimeter Protection
rationale: PS-03 requires physical perimeter protection for premises hosting the cloud service. Access Controls prevents unauthorised physical access to facilities and secure areas.

BSI C5 Criterion: PS-04 Physical Site Access Control
rationale: PS-04 requires access to premises to be restricted to authorised persons, logged and reviewed. Access Controls enforces badging, visitor handling and access logging for secure areas.

BSI C5 Criterion: PS-05 Protection from Fire and Smoke
rationale: PS-05 requires protection of premises and equipment against fire and smoke, including detection and suppression. Environment Controls protects assets against environmental hazards and facility failures.

BSI C5 Criterion: PS-06 Protection Against Interruptions Caused by Power Failures and Other Such Risks
rationale: PS-06 requires protection of premises against power failures and utility interruptions. Environment Controls provides uninterruptible power and generator capacity.

BSI C5 Criterion: OPS-01 Capacity Management - Planning
rationale: OPS-01 requires planning of technical capacity to meet availability commitments. Resilience Controls engineers capacity headroom and graceful degradation into the service.

BSI C5 Criterion: OPS-02 Capacity Management - Monitoring
rationale: OPS-02 requires monitoring of resource usage against planned capacity. Continuous Monitoring provides the automated monitoring that detects deviations from expected resource levels.

BSI C5 Criterion: OPS-03 Capacity Management - Controlling of Resources
rationale: OPS-03 requires resources to be controlled so that capacity shortfalls do not affect availability. Resilience Controls ensures the service continues under load through controlled scaling and prioritisation.

BSI C5 Criterion: OPS-04 Protection Against Malware - Concept
rationale: OPS-04 requires a documented concept for malware protection across systems. Endpoint Security defines and deploys anti-malware and endpoint hardening.

BSI C5 Criterion: OPS-05 Protection Against Malware - Implementation
rationale: OPS-05 requires malware protection to be implemented, kept current and monitored. Endpoint Security operates and monitors anti-malware and EDR tooling on servers, containers and user devices.

BSI C5 Criterion: OPS-06 Data Backup and Recovery - Concept
rationale: OPS-06 requires a documented backup and recovery concept with defined scope and frequency. Disaster Recovery defines backup strategy and restore procedures aligned to RTO and RPO targets.

BSI C5 Criterion: OPS-07 Data Backup and Recovery - Monitoring
rationale: OPS-07 requires backup execution to be monitored and failures handled. Disaster Recovery monitors backup jobs and remediates failures so restore points remain valid.

BSI C5 Criterion: OPS-08 Data Backup and Recovery - Regular Testing
rationale: OPS-08 requires restore procedures to be tested regularly. Disaster Recovery runs tested restores from immutable backups to prove recovery objectives are met.

BSI C5 Criterion: OPS-09 Data Backup and Recovery - Storage
rationale: OPS-09 requires backups to be stored at a separate location with equivalent protection. Disaster Recovery maintains geographically separated, protected backup copies.

BSI C5 Criterion: OPS-10 Logging and Monitoring - Concept
rationale: OPS-10 requires a documented concept for logging and monitoring of security-relevant events. Continuous Monitoring establishes the automated monitoring programme and its coverage.

BSI C5 Criterion: OPS-11 Logging and Monitoring - Metadata Management Concept
rationale: OPS-11 requires a concept for handling log metadata, including customer data within logs. Continuous Monitoring defines what is collected and how monitoring data is governed.

BSI C5 Criterion: OPS-12 Logging and Monitoring - Access, Storage and Deletion
rationale: OPS-12 requires logs to be access-restricted, retained and deleted per policy. Continuous Monitoring protects monitoring data and enforces its retention. Partial alignment: the deletion rules also draw on Classification & Handling.

BSI C5 Criterion: OPS-13 Logging and Monitoring - Identification of Events
rationale: OPS-13 requires logged events to be analysed to identify security incidents and anomalies. Anomaly Detection applies statistical and behavioural analysis to logs to surface unusual activity.

BSI C5 Criterion: OPS-14 Logging and Monitoring - Storage of the Logging Data
rationale: OPS-14 requires logging data to be stored centrally and protected from manipulation. Continuous Monitoring centralises logs in protected storage with integrity controls.

BSI C5 Criterion: OPS-15 Logging and Monitoring - Accountability
rationale: OPS-15 requires logs to attribute actions to individual users and systems. Continuous Monitoring captures attributable events so that activity can be traced to an accountable identity.

BSI C5 Criterion: OPS-16 Logging and Monitoring - Configuration
rationale: OPS-16 requires logging and monitoring configuration to be protected against unauthorised change. Continuous Monitoring governs and protects the monitoring configuration.

BSI C5 Criterion: OPS-17 Logging and Monitoring - Availability of the Monitoring Software
rationale: OPS-17 requires the monitoring tooling itself to be available and its failures detected. Continuous Monitoring monitors the health of its own collection and alerting pipeline.

BSI C5 Criterion: OPS-18 Managing Vulnerabilities, Malfunctions and Errors - Concept
rationale: OPS-18 requires a documented process for identifying, assessing and remediating vulnerabilities within defined timeframes. Cybersecurity Risk Management continuously evaluates vulnerabilities and exposure and drives remediation.

BSI C5 Criterion: OPS-19 Managing Vulnerabilities, Malfunctions and Errors - Penetration Tests
rationale: OPS-19 requires regular penetration tests by qualified testers with findings tracked to closure. Penetration Testing simulates adversarial attacks to evaluate resilience and feeds results into remediation.

BSI C5 Criterion: OPS-20 Managing Vulnerabilities, Malfunctions and Errors - Measurements, Analyses and Assessments of Procedures
rationale: OPS-20 requires regular vulnerability scans and assessment of the effectiveness of the vulnerability process. Vulnerability Testing identifies exploitable weaknesses and measures remediation performance.

BSI C5 Criterion: OPS-23 Managing Vulnerabilities, Malfunctions and Errors - System Hardening
rationale: OPS-23 requires systems to be hardened against defined baselines with unnecessary functions disabled. Platform Security applies hardened configuration to cloud, container and orchestration platforms.

BSI C5 Criterion: IDM-01 Policy for User Accounts and Access Rights
rationale: IDM-01 requires a policy governing user accounts and access rights based on least privilege and need to know. Identity Management defines and enforces the account and access policy for human and machine identities.

BSI C5 Criterion: IDM-02 Granting and Change of User Accounts and Access Rights
rationale: IDM-02 requires accounts and rights to be granted and changed through an approved process. Identity Management runs the provisioning and change workflow with documented approvals.

BSI C5 Criterion: IDM-03 Locking and Withdrawal of User Accounts in the Event of Inactivity or Multiple Failed Logins
rationale: IDM-03 requires accounts to be locked after inactivity or repeated failed logins. Identity Management enforces lockout and inactive-account disablement.

BSI C5 Criterion: IDM-04 Withdraw or Adjust Access Rights as the Task Area Changes
rationale: IDM-04 requires access rights to be withdrawn or adjusted promptly on termination or role change. Identity Management ties access lifecycle to HR events so rights are removed without delay.

BSI C5 Criterion: IDM-05 Regular Review of Access Rights
rationale: IDM-05 requires periodic review of accounts and access rights by owners. Identity Management performs and documents recurring access reviews.

BSI C5 Criterion: IDM-06 Privileged Access Rights
rationale: IDM-06 requires privileged rights to be restricted, personalised, approved and monitored. Identity Management applies privileged access management with separate administrative identities and monitoring.

BSI C5 Criterion: IDM-07 Access to Cloud Customer Data
rationale: IDM-07 requires provider access to customer data to be restricted, justified and logged. Identity Management scopes and logs any administrative access to customer datasets.

BSI C5 Criterion: IDM-08 Confidentiality of Authentication Information
rationale: IDM-08 requires authentication secrets to be protected in issuance, storage and transmission. Identity Management governs credential handling and secret storage for users and service accounts.

BSI C5 Criterion: IDM-09 Authentication Mechanisms
rationale: IDM-09 requires strong authentication, including multi-factor authentication for privileged and remote access. Identity Management enforces MFA and authentication strength appropriate to access risk.

BSI C5 Criterion: CRY-01 Policy for the Use of Encryption Procedures and Key Management
rationale: CRY-01 requires a policy for cryptographic procedures and key management. Cryptographic Management governs approved algorithms, protocols and key lifecycle.

BSI C5 Criterion: CRY-02 Encryption of Data for Transmission (Transport Encryption)
rationale: CRY-02 requires data in transit over public networks to be encrypted with strong protocols. Cryptographic Management enforces approved transport encryption.

BSI C5 Criterion: CRY-03 Encryption of Sensitive Data for Storage
rationale: CRY-03 requires sensitive data at rest to be encrypted. Cryptographic Management enforces approved encryption of stored data and models.

BSI C5 Criterion: CRY-04 Secure Key Management
rationale: CRY-04 requires secure generation, storage, rotation and destruction of keys. Cryptographic Management runs the key management lifecycle with access restricted to authorised roles.

BSI C5 Criterion: COS-01 Technical Safeguards
rationale: COS-01 requires technical safeguards such as firewalls and intrusion detection at network boundaries. Network Security enforces zero-trust boundary controls that prevent lateral movement.

BSI C5 Criterion: COS-03 Monitoring of Connections in the Cloud Service Provider's Network
rationale: COS-03 requires network connections to be monitored for unauthorised traffic. Network Security monitors and controls traffic between zones and detects exfiltration paths.

BSI C5 Criterion: COS-04 Cross-Network Access
rationale: COS-04 requires access between networks of different trust levels to be restricted and controlled. Network Security segments networks and governs cross-zone access.

BSI C5 Criterion: COS-05 Networks for Administration
rationale: COS-05 requires administrative access to use separate, protected networks. Network Security isolates management planes from production and user traffic.

BSI C5 Criterion: COS-06 Segregation of Data Traffic in Jointly Used Network Environments
rationale: COS-06 requires logical separation of customer traffic in shared network environments. Network Security enforces tenant separation on shared infrastructure.

BSI C5 Criterion: COS-07 Documentation of the Network Topology
rationale: COS-07 requires the network topology to be documented and kept current. System Boundaries maintains the boundary and interface diagrams that document the topology.

BSI C5 Criterion: COS-08 Policies for Data Transmission
rationale: COS-08 requires policies governing transmission of data to external parties. Classification & Handling defines transfer rules according to data sensitivity.

BSI C5 Criterion: PI-01 Documentation and Safety of Input and Output Interfaces
rationale: PI-01 requires interfaces used by customers to be documented and secured. System Boundaries maintains the interface inventory and the controls applied at each boundary.

BSI C5 Criterion: PI-02 Contractual Agreements for the Provision of Data
rationale: PI-02 requires contractual commitments on data export and portability to customers. Partial alignment: Transparency governs customer-facing disclosures about the service, but the contractual portability terms themselves sit outside the control.

BSI C5 Criterion: PI-03 Secure Deletion of Data
rationale: PI-03 requires customer data to be securely deleted on contract end. Classification & Handling defines the deletion and sanitisation protocols by data class.

BSI C5 Criterion: DEV-01 Policies for the Development/Procurement of Information Systems
rationale: DEV-01 requires policies and procedures for secure development and procurement of systems. The Software Development Lifecycle embeds secure coding and security requirements across development.

BSI C5 Criterion: DEV-02 Outsourcing of the Development
rationale: DEV-02 requires outsourced development to meet the provider's security requirements under contract and supervision. Third-Party Risk Management writes security requirements into vendor agreements and monitors delivery.

BSI C5 Criterion: DEV-03 Policies for Changes to Information Systems
rationale: DEV-03 requires a documented change process with risk assessment and approval. Change Management ensures changes are risk-assessed, approved and auditable.

BSI C5 Criterion: DEV-06 Testing Changes
rationale: DEV-06 requires changes to be tested, including security tests, before release. Testing plans and executes functional and security tests to find defects before production.

BSI C5 Criterion: DEV-09 Approvals for Provision in the Production Environment
rationale: DEV-09 requires authorised approval before changes reach production. Change Management records approvals and release decisions for every change.

BSI C5 Criterion: DEV-07 Logging of Changes
rationale: DEV-07 requires changes to information systems to be logged so they are traceable. Change Management keeps every change to systems, datasets, models and configurations risk-assessed, approved and auditable, which depends on that change log.

BSI C5 Criterion: DEV-08 Version Control
rationale: DEV-08 requires version control of source code and configuration. Secure Development integrates version control and provenance into the build pipeline.

BSI C5 Criterion: DEV-10 Separation of Environments
rationale: DEV-10 requires development, test and production environments to be separated. Secure Development enforces environment separation and controlled promotion through the pipeline.

BSI C5 Criterion: DEV-06 Testing Changes
rationale: DEV-06 requires security testing of changes before release. Code Scanning performs static and dependency analysis so code reaching production is free of known defects.

BSI C5 Criterion: SSO-01 Policies and Instructions for Controlling and Monitoring Third Parties
rationale: SSO-01 requires a policy setting security requirements for subservice organisations and suppliers. Supply-Chain Policies sets the standards suppliers must meet through the contract lifecycle.

BSI C5 Criterion: SSO-01 Policies and Instructions for Controlling and Monitoring Third Parties
rationale: SSO-01 requires risk-based control of third parties, including contractual security requirements. Third-Party Risk Management assesses suppliers and embeds requirements in agreements.

BSI C5 Criterion: SSO-04 Monitoring of Compliance with Requirements
rationale: SSO-04 requires ongoing monitoring of third parties' compliance with contractual security requirements. Monitor Third Parties continuously monitors vendor posture and compliance.

BSI C5 Criterion: SSO-05 Exit Strategy for the Receipt of Services
rationale: SSO-05 requires an exit strategy for critical third-party services. Third-Party Risk Management maintains exit and transition plans as part of vendor risk treatment.

BSI C5 Criterion: SIM-01 Policy for Security Incident Management
rationale: SIM-01 requires a documented security incident management policy with roles and procedures. Response & Resilience Policies establishes the incident response policy.

BSI C5 Criterion: SIM-02 Processing of Security Incidents
rationale: SIM-02 requires incidents to be handled through defined steps from detection to closure. Incident Response: Cybersecurity coordinates the technical response across infrastructure and applications.

BSI C5 Criterion: SIM-03 Documentation and Reporting of Security Incidents
rationale: SIM-03 requires incidents to be documented and reported to affected customers and authorities. Incident Management records incidents and drives classification, escalation and notification.

BSI C5 Criterion: SIM-04 Duty of the Users to Report Security Incidents to a Central Body
rationale: SIM-04 requires personnel to report security events to a central body. Reporting Channels provides accessible channels for reporting incidents and concerns.

BSI C5 Criterion: SIM-05 Evaluation and Learning Process
rationale: SIM-05 requires incidents to be evaluated and lessons applied to improve controls. Incident Lessons Learned turns every incident into tracked control improvements.

BSI C5 Criterion: BCM-01 Top Management Responsibility
rationale: BCM-01 requires top management to own business continuity management. Business Continuity maintains the continuity programme with executive ownership.

BSI C5 Criterion: BCM-02 Business Impact Analysis Policies and Instructions
rationale: BCM-02 requires a business impact analysis to identify critical processes and recovery parameters. Business Continuity derives its strategies from BIA-defined priorities.

BSI C5 Criterion: BCM-03 Planning Business Continuity
rationale: BCM-03 requires continuity and recovery plans that meet the recovery parameters. Disaster Recovery restores systems and data to defined RTO and RPO.

BSI C5 Criterion: BCM-03 Planning Business Continuity
rationale: BCM-03 requires plans to maintain critical operations during disruption. Business Continuity (RESPOND) keeps critical operations running during incident response and recovery.

BSI C5 Criterion: BCM-04 Verification, Updating and Testing of the Business Continuity
rationale: BCM-04 requires continuity plans to be tested and updated regularly. Tabletop Exercises (BCDR) tests continuity, recovery and response readiness through structured simulations.

BSI C5 Criterion: COM-01 Identification of Applicable Legal, Regulatory, Self-Imposed or Contractual Requirements
rationale: COM-01 requires applicable legal, regulatory and contractual requirements to be identified and kept current. Cybersecurity Regulatory Compliance aligns controls to those obligations and maintains continuous compliance.

BSI C5 Criterion: COM-01 Identification of Applicable Legal, Regulatory, Self-Imposed or Contractual Requirements
rationale: COM-01 requires the set of applicable requirements to be determined. Regulatory Scope determines which legal, contractual and customer requirements the management system must address.

BSI C5 Criterion: COM-02 Policy for Planning and Conducting Audits
rationale: COM-02 requires a policy for planning and conducting audits of the ISMS. Internal Audit provides the chartered, independent audit function and plan.

BSI C5 Criterion: COM-03 Internal Audits of the Information Security Management System
rationale: COM-03 requires regular internal audits of control design and effectiveness. Internal Audit: Security Audit independently assesses ISMS control design and operation.

BSI C5 Criterion: COM-04 Information on Information Security Performance and Management Assessment of the ISMS
rationale: COM-04 requires security performance to be reported to management for assessment. Reporting delivers structured, risk-informed reporting to executives and the Board.

BSI C5 Criterion: INQ-01 Legal Assessment of Investigative Inquiries
rationale: INQ-01 requires investigative inquiries from authorities to be legally assessed before any disclosure. Law Enforcement Partners defines the procedures and authority for engaging with law enforcement requests.

BSI C5 Criterion: INQ-02 Informing Cloud Customers about Investigation Requests
rationale: INQ-02 requires affected customers to be informed about investigation requests where legally permitted. Partial alignment: Recovery Activity & Restoration governs customer-facing incident communication, which carries this notification, but it is not specific to investigations.

BSI C5 Criterion: INQ-03 Conditions for Access to or Disclosure of Data in Investigation Requests
rationale: INQ-03 requires disclosure to authorities only under defined legal conditions. Cybersecurity Regulatory Compliance tracks the legal obligations that condition such disclosures.

BSI C5 Criterion: PSS-04 Error Handling and Logging Mechanisms
rationale: PSS-04 requires the cloud service to handle errors securely and log security-relevant events. Platform Security hardens runtime platforms and their error handling and logging.

BSI C5 Criterion: PSS-06 Session Management
rationale: PSS-06 requires secure session handling in the service. Platform Security applies secure configuration to session management of hosted services.

BSI C5 Criterion: PSS-08 Roles and Rights Concept
rationale: PSS-08 requires a roles and rights concept for cloud customers' users. Identity Management defines role-based access for customer-facing identities.

BSI C5 Criterion: PSS-05 Authentication Mechanisms
rationale: PSS-05 requires strong authentication mechanisms for the service. Identity Management enforces authentication strength and MFA for service users.

BSI C5 Criterion: PSS-11 Images for Virtual Machines and Containers
rationale: PSS-11 requires VM and container images to be hardened, provenance-checked and kept current. Platform Security secures image provenance and hardened configuration for build and deploy planes.

BSI C5 Criterion: PSS-12 Locations of Data Processing and Storage
rationale: PSS-12 requires the cloud service provider to disclose the locations where customer data is processed and stored. System Boundaries records the physical and jurisdictional boundaries of processing so that disclosure is accurate.

BSI C5 Criterion: PSS-12 Locations of Data Processing and Storage
rationale: PSS-12 requires the cloud service provider to disclose the locations where customer data is processed and stored. Transparency governs publication of that location and jurisdiction information to customers. Partial alignment: the ARISE control is written for AI disclosures.

BSI C5 Criterion: INQ-02 Informing Cloud Customers about Investigation Requests
rationale: INQ-02 requires cloud customers to be informed about investigation requests concerning their data where legally permitted. Transparency governs that external communication. Partial alignment: the ARISE control is written for AI disclosures.

BSI C5 Criterion: OIS-03 Interfaces and Dependencies
rationale: OIS-03 requires interfaces and dependencies between the cloud service, its components and third parties to be identified and documented. System Boundaries establishes those technical boundaries and interfaces so controls can be applied and audited.

BSI C5 Criterion: COS-02 Security Requirements for Connections in the Cloud Service Provider's Network
rationale: COS-02 requires security requirements for connections within the provider network to be defined and enforced. Network Security designs the zero-trust segmentation and traffic rules that implement them.

BSI C5 Criterion: SSO-02 Risk Assessment of Service Providers and Suppliers
rationale: SSO-02 requires a risk assessment of service providers and suppliers before engagement and at intervals. Third-Party Risk Management performs that assessment and tracks its findings.

BSI C5 Criterion: SSO-03 Directory of Service Providers and Suppliers
rationale: SSO-03 requires a directory of service providers and suppliers with the services they deliver. Supply Chain Risk maintains the inventory of suppliers of software, models, datasets and cloud services that risk management depends on.

BSI C5 Criterion: OPS-21 Involvement of Cloud Customers in the Event of Incidents
rationale: OPS-21 requires cloud customers to be involved and informed in the event of incidents affecting them. Recovery Activity & Restoration provides customers timely updates on restoration and remediation status.

BSI C5 Criterion: OPS-24 Separation of Datasets in the Cloud Infrastructure
rationale: OPS-24 requires separation of customer datasets in the shared cloud infrastructure. Platform Security hardens the multi-tenant platform so tenant isolation is enforced at build and runtime.

BSI C5 Criterion: PSS-02 Identification of Vulnerabilities of the Cloud Service
rationale: PSS-02 requires the provider to identify vulnerabilities in the cloud service it delivers. Vulnerability Testing identifies and drives mitigation of exploitable weaknesses in systems and applications.

BSI C5 Criterion: PSS-03 Online Register of Known Vulnerabilities
rationale: PSS-03 requires an online register of known vulnerabilities for cloud customers. Public Updates / Disclosures manages approved external communications about security issues.

BSI C5 Criterion: PSS-09 Authorisation Mechanisms
rationale: PSS-09 requires authorisation mechanisms in the cloud service that enforce the roles and rights concept. Identity Management enforces least privilege and separation of duties for human and machine entities.

BSI C5 Criterion: INQ-04 Limiting Access to or Disclosure of Data in Investigation Requests
rationale: INQ-04 requires access to or disclosure of data in investigation requests to be limited to what is legally required. Cybersecurity Regulatory Compliance keeps disclosure practice aligned with legal obligations.

BSI C5 Criterion: DEV-04 Safety Training and Awareness Programme Regarding Continuous Software Delivery
rationale: DEV-04 requires a security training and awareness programme for personnel involved in continuous software delivery. Cybersecurity Training delivers role-based security awareness to those teams.

BSI C5 Criterion: DEV-05 Risk Assessment, Categorisation and Prioritisation of Changes
rationale: DEV-05 requires changes to be risk-assessed, categorised and prioritised before implementation. Change Management ensures every change is risk-assessed and approved.
